newsitem.title: USA: Dow soars; ends just short of new high.
newsitem.headline: Dow soars; ends just short of new high.

text.p: The stock market stormed higher Wednesday as the Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates steady lifted secondary indexes into record ground but left the Dow Jones industrial average just short of a new high.
The blue-chip Dow ended up 73.05 points at 7,795.38, which was just below its June 20 record close of 7,796.51.
In the broader market, advancing issues swamped declines 1,837 to 961 on active volume of 526 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks, New York Stock Exchange Composite and Nasdaq Composite indices set record highs.
The fierce rally caught many analysts by surprise, coming as it did after a Fed decision that was nearly universally anticipated on Wall Street.
Initially, investors appeared to shrug off the news, but in the final minutes of the session, a series of buy programmes virtually seized control of the market.

"It's like a game of hot potato where no one wants to get caught holding cash," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany. "Whether it's mutual funds or brokerage firms or whomever, we've all learned it's no fun to get caught holding cash in a rising market."
The bond market also shot higher, with the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond up 12/32, lowering its yield to 6.71 percent from 6.74 percent Tuesday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
The rally in stocks was also remarkable in light of economic indicators still looming -- the closely watched monthly payrolls and wage data, scheduled for release early Thursday.
The report is considered one of the most important leading inflation indicators and when the figures have revealed unexpected strength, Wall Street's reaction has been swift and severe.
A year ago in July, the jobs numbers served as the trigger point for the market's stiff summer-long correction.
However, there was some speculation on Wall Street that the Fed's decision to hold the line on interest rates on Wednesday foreshadowed a tame report on Thursday.

"There's no doubt in my mind the Fed has already had a look at those numbers," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Kemper Funds. "It probably means those numbers are going to be tame."

Economists surveyed by Reuters expect the report will show June payrolls rose by 222,000 jobs, up from a 138,000 gain in May. The nation's unemployment rate is expected to hold steady at 4.8 pecent and wages are forecast to rise by 0.4 percent, up from 0.3 percent a month ago.

Once the jobs report is released, traders will have little time to register their response. Markets will hold an abbreviated session Thursday ahead of the Independence Day holiday, with the NYSE, AMEX and Nasdaq all slated to close at 1300 EDT (1700 GMT).
Among Dow components, Walt Disney Co. fell 1-11/16 to 76-7/8 after the brokerage house Deutsche Morgan Grenfell downgraded the shares to hold, citing concern over ratings at Disney's ABC TV network.

In other individual issues, Pennzoil Co. fell 15/16 to 74-7/16 after the integrated oil company rejected a hostile $84 per share takeover bid from Union Pacific Resources Group Inc. Union Pacific Resources fell 1/16 to 24-15/16.
Peritus Software Services Inc. was the top percentage gainer on Nasdaq, surging 10-3/4 or 67 percent to 26-3/4 in its first trading.
Peritus makes software for large-scale computer systems changes like those associated with the year 2000 changeover and the planned conversion to a unified European currency.
Nike Inc. fell 5/8 to 57-3/8 after the footwear maker late Tuesday reported second-quarter earnings that were slightly below analysts' estimates.
Several other companies fell sharply after warning about upcoming earnings disappointments.
Friedman's Inc. tumbled 6-11/16 to 16-1/16 and IKOS Systems Inc. slid 5-1/4 to 15-1/8 after both companies announced quarterly results that fell short of expectations.

Networking stocks were strong, leading a rally in technology stocks, with Ascend Communications Inc. rising 5-5/16 to 49-1/16 and 3Com Corp. up 3-11/16 to 48-1/8. Both companies were upgraded by Wall Street firms.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 17.36 points to 1,455.61, a new high.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 13.00 to 904.03, a new high. The American Stock Exchange index rose 4.45 to 630.06.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 5.70 to 471.71, a record. The average share was up 54 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 8,541.510 up 100.084 or 1.19 percent.
